components.css: .ds-switch{--surface:#fff;--well:#f6f6f7;--ink:#1b1b1f;--text:#2e2e33;--muted:#6b6b75;--line:#e5e5e8;--track:#ececef;--bar:#c2c2c8;--accent:#0a5651;--focus:#0b57d0;display:inline-flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;color:var(--muted);font:12px/1.45 system-ui,-apple-system,"Segoe UI",sans-serif;cursor:pointer}.ds-switch input{appearance:none;position:relative;margin:0;width:28px;height:16px;border-radius:999px;background:#8a8a94;cursor:pointer;transition:background-color 150ms ease}.ds-switch input::before{content:"";position:absolute;top:2px;left:2px;width:12px;height:12px;border-radius:50%;background:#fff;box-shadow:0 1px 2px rgb(0 0 0 / .2);transition:transform 150ms cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1)}.ds-switch input:checked{background:var(--accent)}.ds-switch input:checked::before{transform:translateX(12px)}.ds-switch input:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--focus);outline-offset:2px;border-radius:999px}

narrative.overview:
Impulse looks like it shipped with the browser. The side panel uses Chrome's own side-panel language: the system font at 13px, one neutral gray scale, 1px hairlines, flat 32px list rows, and Linear-level care with density and numbers. There is no themed world, no brand illustration, and no card grid. Chrome's side-panel header already shows the product name and icon, so the panel itself has no title.

The overlay is a calm friction screen in the style of Opal and one sec. A frosted neutral scrim covers the blurred post. On it sit one number at display size, one dry line of plain sentences, and a quiet "Show anyway" that is meant to feel like a small cost. It uses the same type stack and gray scale as the panel, so both surfaces read as one system even though one lives inside third-party pages.

Light and dark follow `prefers-color-scheme` on both surfaces. Motion is limited to state changes (150ms) and a deliberately slow 500ms fade when a post gets blurred.
keyCharacteristics: System UI type, 13px base, tabular figures for every number.
One neutral scale plus one accent, the icon teal, used only for selection and the switch.
Hairlines and flat rows instead of cards and shadows.
A single lead fact per surface, stated in plain sentences.
The overlay is the same in every host: namespaced, contained, and quiet.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Teal means "you chose to block this." It marks selection and the on state, nothing else. No second accent, no teal on the overlay.

rules.name: The Monochrome Exit Rule
rules.body: "Show anyway" uses only scrim grays. It never gets the accent, a fill, or any color that invites a click.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Every amount and count uses tabular numerals so columns and live updates do not shift.

rules.name: The Plain Sentence Rule
rules.body: Copy is plain sentences. No fragments separated by periods, no late-night count in the panel, no estimate blurb. The estimate is labeled with the words "est. saved" right next to its figure.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Separate things with a 1px hairline or a well tone. Don't use cards, borders on all four sides, or shadows to group.

rules.name: The Contained Overlay Rule
rules.body: The overlay lives inside each blurred host's stacking context. Every overlay class is `ss-` prefixed, starts from `all: initial`/`all: unset`, and uses `!important`, so host pages are never affected.

dos: **Do** use the system font stack at 13px with tabular figures for every number.
**Do** keep the icon teal for selection and the on state only.
**Do** separate content with 1px hairlines and flat 32px rows.
**Do** lead each surface with one fact in plain sentences, and label estimates with "est. saved."
**Do** follow `prefers-color-scheme` on both panel and overlay, using the paired dark tokens.
**Do** cap blocked groups at 3 and show the count in the Block header.
**Do** fade overlays and blur in over 500ms. Use 150ms for state changes.
**Do** prefix every overlay class with `ss-` and keep it inside the host's stacking context.
donts: **Don't** add an "Impulse" heading inside the panel. Chrome's side-panel header already shows the name and icon.
**Don't** give "Show anyway" color, a fill, a shadow, or a primary-button look.
**Don't** use cards, metric tiles or a hero-metric layout. Impact stays on one inline line.
**Don't** write period-separated fragments, a late-night count, or an estimate blurb in the panel.
**Don't** add a second accent or a themed palette. The icon's colors are not binding for the UI.
**Don't** show sample data without the notice and the "Sample data" label.
